# Tests CI knows about but does not run. TEMPORARY — this list should shrink.
#
# How this list was produced, rather than guessed: every test class in the repo
# was run on its own, in its own JVM, with a 1500m heap and a 10 second budget
# for the test run itself (surefire's forkedProcessTimeoutInSeconds, so maven
# startup and compilation are not on the clock). 194 classes were measured; the
# 96 that passed became the initial CI set and the 98 below what it skipped.
# Classes fixed since have been deleted from this list, which is now 94 entries.
# The number CI runs is deliberately not recorded here: it also grows whenever a
# test class is added, so any figure written down goes stale on its own.
# Each is grouped by how it actually failed.
#
# Nothing here is a regression from enabling CI. All of it was already broken,
# already dependent on infrastructure nobody provides, or already too heavy.
#
# This is not the same thing as .github/perf-test-excludes.txt. Perf harnesses
# are excluded permanently and on purpose. Everything here is meant to come back:
# fix a class, delete its line, and CI picks it up on the next run.
#
# Nothing here is skipped for a local `mvn -Dskip-tests=false test`, so all of it
# stays runnable while it is being fixed.
#
# Only whole-line comments are safe in this file: surefire skips lines starting
# with '#' but would read anything trailing a pattern as part of the pattern.
#
# Not listed, and not runnable either way: **/integration/*.java, which the pom
# excludes outright.
#
# One caveat for whoever revives these: many of the crashes and OOMs likely share
# a root cause. OrderBookTest.createInstruments populates the *static*
# InstrumentCache from @Before and nothing clears it, so classes extending that
# fixture leak into each other. CI now runs one JVM per class, which contains the
# damage but does not fix it. Fixing the fixture may clear a large block of this
# list at once.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Kill the JVM they run in (51)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The forked test JVM dies without producing a report — surefire reports "The
# forked VM terminated without properly saying goodbye". Mostly classes that reach
# for infrastructure that is not there (Kafka, Zookeeper, exchange endpoints, raw
# sockets) or that call System.exit. A class that can kill its JVM is the reason
# CI runs one JVM per class: without that, one of these takes every class
# scheduled after it down with it.

# Exhaust the heap (6)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Die with "Java heap space" in a JVM of their own with -Xmx1500m, so this is
# not the shared-fixture accumulation that per-class forking already solves. These
# genuinely need more memory than a runner should be asked for, or they leak.
